item.title: Self-Hosted Linux Kernel Dynamic Tracing: trace-cmd vs SystemTap vs perf probe
item.description: Kernel dynamic tracing allows you to observe running Linux systems in real time — probing kernel functions, tracking system calls, measuring latency, and diagnosing performance bottlenecks without recompiling the kernel or restarting services. Three major toolchains dominate this space: trace-cmd (the ftrace frontend), SystemTap (Red Hat’s scripting-based tracer), and perf probe (the perf subsystem’s dynamic instrumentation interface).
